title: How to Convert HTML to Markdown: Quick Guide (2026)
description: Learn how to convert HTML to Markdown easily. Free online tool, code examples, and tips for cleaning up web content for editing.

sections.heading: Why Convert HTML to Markdown?
sections.content: HTML is the language of the web, but it is verbose and difficult to edit by hand. Markdown offers a cleaner, more readable alternative for writing and editing content. Converting HTML to Markdown is useful when you want to migrate blog posts to a static site generator, clean up content copied from a CMS, extract text from web pages for documentation, or switch from HTML email templates to Markdown for easier maintenance. This guide covers the best methods to convert HTML to Markdown using free online tools, programming libraries, and command-line utilities. You will learn how to preserve formatting while stripping away unnecessary HTML tags and attributes.

sections.heading: Method 1: Free Online HTML to Markdown Converter
sections.content: The fastest way to convert HTML to Markdown is using a browser-based converter. These tools work instantly without installing software. Simply paste your HTML code into the input area, click convert, and copy the clean Markdown output. Quality converters handle common HTML elements like headings, paragraphs, lists, links, images, and tables. They also strip unnecessary attributes and inline styles that clutter the output. sections.heading: Method 2: Using Turndown in JavaScript Projects
sections.content: Turndown is the most popular JavaScript library for converting HTML to Markdown. It works in both Node.js and browser environments. Install it with npm install turndown, then convert HTML with a few lines of code: import TurndownService from turndown; const turndownService = new TurndownService(); const markdown = turndownService.turndown(htmlString);. Turndown is highly configurable. You can customize how specific HTML elements are converted using rules and filters. The library handles GitHub-flavored Markdown tables, code blocks, and strikethrough text. For browser use, include the CDN script or bundle it with your application using webpack or rollup.

sections.heading: Method 3: Pandoc for Batch Conversion
sections.content: Pandoc excels at batch converting multiple HTML files to Markdown. Install Pandoc on your system, then run: pandoc input.html -o output.md. For an entire directory of HTML files, use a shell loop: for file in *.html; do pandoc "$file" -o "${file%.html}.md"; done. Pandoc supports various Markdown flavors including strict Markdown, GitHub-flavored Markdown, and CommonMark. You can specify the output format with -t markdown_strict or -t gfm. For cleaner output, add --wrap=none to prevent line wrapping and --strip-comments to remove HTML comments. Pandoc also handles conversion from URLs directly: pandoc -s -r html https://example.com -o output.md.

sections.heading: Cleaning Up HTML Before Conversion
sections.content: Not all HTML converts cleanly to Markdown. Preparing your HTML before conversion produces better results. Remove script tags, style tags, and inline styles that have no Markdown equivalent. Strip class and id attributes that are not needed in the final output. Ensure heading tags follow a logical hierarchy without skipping levels. Convert HTML entities to their character equivalents for readability. Remove empty paragraphs and redundant line breaks. If your HTML comes from a WYSIWYG editor or Microsoft Word, it may contain bloated markup. Running it through an HTML cleaner first produces cleaner Markdown output. Several online HTML cleaners can preprocess your code before conversion.

sections.heading: Handling Complex HTML Elements
sections.content: Some HTML elements do not have direct Markdown equivalents and require special handling. Tables convert to Markdown table syntax, but complex tables with colspan or rowspan may lose structure. Consider keeping these as HTML within Markdown files. Definition lists, footnotes, and citations require Markdown extensions that not all parsers support. Embedded content like iframes and videos typically remain as HTML. Forms and interactive elements have no Markdown representation and should stay in HTML. When converting documentation with code examples, ensure language identifiers are preserved for syntax highlighting. Always review the converted Markdown to catch any elements that did not translate correctly.
